+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+DATA = ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet"
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+con.execute("SET threads TO 4")
+yearly = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           count(*) AS city_crash_rows,
+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE borough IS NULL) AS null_borough_rows,
+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN') AS brooklyn_crashes,
+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN'
+               AND (number_of_pedestrians_injured IS NULL
+                    OR number_of_pedestrians_killed IS NULL)) AS null_pedestrian_values,
+           sum(number_of_pedestrians_injured) FILTER (WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN') AS pedestrians_injured,
+           sum(number_of_pedestrians_killed) FILTER (WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN') AS pedestrians_killed,
+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN'
+               AND number_of_pedestrians_injured + number_of_pedestrians_killed > 0)
+               AS pedestrian_casualty_crashes
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """,
+    [str(DATA)],
+).df()
+
+# Compare complete calendar years only; 2012 and 2026 are partial in the file.
+years = yearly[(yearly.year >= 2013) & (yearly.year <= 2025)].copy()
+years["pedestrian_casualties"] = years.pedestrians_injured + years.pedestrians_killed
+years["pedestrian_casualty_crash_pct"] = (
+    years.pedestrian_casualty_crashes / years.brooklyn_crashes * 100
+)
+years["null_borough_pct_of_city_rows"] = years.null_borough_rows / years.city_crash_rows * 100
+years.to_csv(OUT / "annual_computed_values.csv", index=False)
+
+plt.rcParams.update({
+    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",
+    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
+    "axes.titlesize": 17,
+    "axes.labelsize": 11,
+    "xtick.labelsize": 9,
+    "ytick.labelsize": 10,
+    "figure.facecolor": "white",
+    "axes.facecolor": "white",
+})
+
+def finish(ax, title, subtitle, ylabel, source_note):
+    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", pad=28)
+    ax.text(0, 1.02, subtitle, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=10, color="#4b5563", va="bottom")
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.set_xlabel("")
+    ax.set_xticks(years.year)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=0, length=0, pad=7)
+    ax.spines[["top", "right", "left"]].set_visible(False)
+    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#cbd5e1")
+    ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e5e7eb", linewidth=0.8)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    ax.text(0, -0.23, source_note, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8, color="#6b7280", va="top")
+
+# Option 1: count the people injured and killed, retaining the severity breakdown.
+v1 = years[["year", "pedestrians_injured", "pedestrians_killed", "pedestrian_casualties", "brooklyn_crashes"]].copy()
+v1.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6.2))
+ax.bar(years.year, years.pedestrians_injured, color="#2b6cb0", label="Pedestrians injured")
+ax.bar(years.year, years.pedestrians_killed, bottom=years.pedestrians_injured,
+       color="#c53030", label="Pedestrians killed")
+ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right", ncol=2)
+finish(ax, "Pedestrian casualties in Brooklyn have fallen since 2013",
+       "People injured or killed in police-reported crashes · complete calendar years",
+       "Pedestrians injured or killed", "Source: NYC motor vehicle crash records. Counts are people, not unique individuals; borough must be recorded as Brooklyn.")
+ax.annotate(f"{int(years.iloc[0].pedestrian_casualties):,}",
+            (years.iloc[0].year, years.iloc[0].pedestrian_casualties), xytext=(5, 8), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=9)
+ax.annotate(f"{int(years.iloc[-1].pedestrian_casualties):,}",
+            (years.iloc[-1].year, years.iloc[-1].pedestrian_casualties), xytext=(-25, 8), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=9)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Option 2: use pedestrian deaths alone to emphasize the most severe outcome.
+v2 = years[["year", "pedestrians_killed", "brooklyn_crashes"]].copy()
+v2.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6.2))
+ax.plot(years.year, years.pedestrians_killed, color="#9b2c2c", linewidth=2.8, marker="o", markersize=5)
+ax.fill_between(years.year, years.pedestrians_killed, color="#fed7d7", alpha=0.65)
+finish(ax, "Pedestrian deaths in Brooklyn: year to year",
+       "Fatalities in police-reported crashes · complete calendar years",
+       "Pedestrians killed", "Source: NYC motor vehicle crash records. Counts are people, not unique individuals; borough must be recorded as Brooklyn.")
+for row in (years.iloc[0], years.iloc[-1]):
+    ax.annotate(f"{int(row.pedestrians_killed):,}", (row.year, row.pedestrians_killed),
+                xytext=(0, 9), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=9)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Option 3: within-crash share controls for changes in the number of reported crashes.
+v3 = years[["year", "pedestrian_casualty_crashes", "brooklyn_crashes", "pedestrian_casualty_crash_pct"]].copy()
+v3.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False)
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6.2))
+ax.plot(years.year, years.pedestrian_casualty_crash_pct, color="#276749", linewidth=2.8, marker="o", markersize=5)
+ax.fill_between(years.year, years.pedestrian_casualty_crash_pct, color="#c6f6d5", alpha=0.7)
+finish(ax, "Pedestrian-injury crashes as a share of Brooklyn crashes",
+       "Brooklyn crash records involving at least one pedestrian injured or killed · complete calendar years",
+       "Share of Brooklyn crashes (%)", "Source: NYC motor vehicle crash records. The denominator is all records assigned to Brooklyn, not pedestrian trips or exposure.")
+for row in (years.iloc[0], years.iloc[-1]):
+    ax.annotate(f"{row.pedestrian_casualty_crash_pct:.1f}%", (row.year, row.pedestrian_casualty_crash_pct),
+                xytext=(0, 9), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=9)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_3.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+plt.close(fig)
+
+null_share_min = years.null_borough_pct_of_city_rows.min()
+null_share_max = years.null_borough_pct_of_city_rows.max()
+null_share_all = years.null_borough_rows.sum() / years.city_crash_rows.sum() * 100
+partial = yearly[yearly.year.isin([2012, 2026])][["year", "city_crash_rows"]].to_dict("records")
+
+def change(metric):
+    start, end = float(years.iloc[0][metric]), float(years.iloc[-1][metric])
+    delta = end - start
+    pct = (end / start - 1) * 100
+    return start, end, delta, pct
+
+c1 = change("pedestrian_casualties")
+c2 = change("pedestrians_killed")
+c3 = change("pedestrian_casualty_crash_pct")
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Pedestrians injured plus pedestrians killed in Brooklyn crashes (annual count)",
+            "denominator": "None; annual casualty count",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Stacked annual bar chart (injured and killed)",
+            "reason": "Total pedestrian casualties provide a direct measure of the human toll, while the stacked bars retain the distinction between injuries and deaths.",
+            "probability": 0.5,
+            "answer": f"Annual pedestrian casualties fell from {int(c1[0]):,} in 2013 to {int(c1[1]):,} in 2025, a decrease of {abs(c1[3]):.1f}%, indicating improvement in the recorded toll.",
+            "interpretation": f"This framing answers whether the recorded number of pedestrians hurt or killed in Brooklyn crashes declined, and the chart shows {int(c1[0]):,} casualties in 2013 versus {int(c1[1]):,} in 2025 ({abs(c1[3]):.1f}% fewer). It is defensible because injury and death counts measure the direct human toll, with deaths distinguished in the bars. It cannot establish risk per pedestrian trip, explain causes, or isolate changes in traffic or walking exposure. The analysis uses complete years 2013–2025, excludes 2012 and 2026 (each partial in the file), excludes non-Brooklyn and NULL-borough rows (NULL borough accounts for {null_share_all:.1f}% of NYC rows across these years; year by year {null_share_min:.1f}%–{null_share_max:.1f}%), and excludes no Brooklyn rows for NULL pedestrian counts (0 of {int(years.brooklyn_crashes.sum()):,} Brooklyn records had either count missing).",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Pedestrians killed in Brooklyn crashes (annual count)",
+            "denominator": "None; annual death count",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Annual line chart",
+            "reason": "Fatalities are an unambiguous severe outcome and can reveal whether the gravest pedestrian harm has moved differently from total injuries.",
+            "probability": 0.25,
+            "answer": f"Recorded pedestrian deaths changed from {int(c2[0]):,} in 2013 to {int(c2[1]):,} in 2025 ({c2[3]:+.1f}%), so this severe-outcome measure {'improved' if c2[3] < 0 else 'worsened'}.",
+            "interpretation": f"This framing answers whether the most severe recorded pedestrian outcome has improved; deaths moved from {int(c2[0]):,} in 2013 to {int(c2[1]):,} in 2025 ({c2[3]:+.1f}%). It is defensible because fatality counts focus on severity rather than combining deaths with nonfatal injuries. +        },
+        {
+            "id": 3,
+            "metric": "Brooklyn crashes with at least one pedestrian injured or killed, as a share of Brooklyn crashes",
+            "denominator": "All crash records with borough recorded as Brooklyn in the same year",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Annual line chart of percentage",
+            "reason": "A within-crash share adjusts for changes in the volume of Brooklyn crash records, while directly comparing the relative frequency of pedestrian-casualty crashes.",
+            "probability": 0.25,
